prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: The API now requires keys with viewer, cook and manager roles, writes an audit entry for every change request, and has a managers-only `GET /audit`; `npm test` (30 tests) and `npm run lint` pass. Requests without a key or with an unknown key get 401 `unauthorized`, and a known key whose role is too low gets 403 `forbidden`, both in the usual error shape. Cooks may cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts; starting and finishing a stock-take is for managers. Each route that needs more than the default carries its role in the route entry; otherwise GET needs viewer and every other method needs manager. An audit entry records time, key name, method, path and status. It is written for every request other than GET made with a known key, including 403s and other failures, but not for 401s, so anonymous callers cannot fill the data file. The seed has one key per role. The existing tests send the manager key through `tests/helpers.js`, and I added `tests/auth.test.js` for 401, 403, the cook permissions and the audit. Three things to know: (1) I left `data/db.json` alone because the task named only the seed, and it has no `apiKeys`, so `npm start` on it answers 401 to every request until you add keys to it. (2) I did not bump the schema version. `apiKeys` and `audit` are optional collections, like `stocktakes` already is, and a bump would break the CLI test that expects "schema 1 → 2". (3) A successful change request now writes the data file twice: once in the route and once for the audit entry.

check.why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
